shared_contract.coefficient_set: P_q={0,+/-2^r:r=0,...,q-1}; real and imaginary parts independently belong to P_q
shared_contract.L: number of nontrivial constant-multiplication positions when the factor chain acts layer by layer on an input vector; no sharing across rows or layers
shared_contract.K: positive integer count of all N-by-N linear layers that can expand support; pure permutations are recorded separately and excluded

seed_policy_global.rule: Run every stochastic candidate at every registered instance under all three seeds; do not cancel remaining seeds after a good run.

budget_global.fairness: For the same (problem,N,K,q), all stochastic candidates receive the same wall-clock and sweep caps on the same hardware.

validation_levels.L0: Unitary target and zero-based index checks; verify F4 tensor F8 differs from F32; hand-check N=2; verify multiplication order, row support, P_q membership, K, L, C, and the support lower bound.
validation_levels.L1: Run every deterministic baseline at all registered sizes and save target/factor hashes plus independent RMSE recomputation.
validation_levels.L2: Run baseline and two challengers under equal instance budgets and seeds; retain PASS, TIMEOUT, INFEASIBLE, CRASH, and CONSTRAINT_FAIL records.
validation_levels.L3: Stress random seed, initialization order, floating tolerance, multiplication association, and boundary K/q; report best, median, and worst feasible metrics.
validation_levels.L4: Ablate hierarchical initialization, support reconnection, and discrete polishing; compare fixed Butterfly support against reconnectable support.

global_stop_rule: Stop at the instance budget or after 50 complete sweeps with independent RMSE improvement below 1e-10; q5 feasibility never permits skipping the remaining registered seeds.
global_failure_rule: Constraint violation, NaN/Inf, target hash mismatch, search-versus-independent RMSE discrepancy above 1e-10, timeout, or crash is a retained failure record. Uncomputed metrics are null, never zero.
global_fallback_rule: If no challenger strictly beats a feasible baseline under the registered ordering, retain the baseline. For q5, if no run reaches RMSE<=0.1, report no feasible winner within budget.

problems.scope_note: Finite instances validate implementation; claims for every t>=1 require a general construction or proof.
problems.constraints: beta=1; every counted layer is N-by-N and has at most two nonzeros per row; coefficients are unrestricted complex numbers; pure permutations are separate; q=16 only for C.
problems.data_split: No statistical split: the complete deterministic target matrix is used. All candidates receive identical target bytes; independent verification regenerates the matrix from the formula.
problems.seed_policy: Baseline seed 0; challengers use seeds 17,43,71 at every (N,K).
problems.budget: Global segmented budget: baseline 60 s; challengers 300/900/1800 s for N<=16/N=32/N=64 with corresponding sweep caps.
problems.tie_breaker: RMSE values within 1e-12 tie; then lower C, lower K, lower wall_clock_s, lower seed, lexical candidate id.
problems.failure_rule: Apply global failure rule; a claimed exact construction also fails if independent max-entry residual exceeds 1e-10.
problems.fallback_rule: Use q1-b0-scaled-radix2 unless a feasible challenger has strictly smaller RMSE, or equal RMSE within tolerance and lower C/K.

candidates.method: Construct a radix-2 Butterfly chain, record bit reversal as a pure permutation, absorb 1/sqrt(N) into one counted factor so that the product equals the unitary F_N at beta=1, then recount L on the scaled factors.
assumptions: N is a power of two
unrestricted complex coefficients
the absorbed scale is part of one counted linear layer
variables: factor entries induced by the analytic construction
candidates.objective: Provide a feasible exact RMSE-zero reference and its D-005 L/C count.
candidates.stop_condition: Deterministic construction completes or reaches 60 seconds.
candidates.complexity: Construction and sparse application O(N log N); dense independent matrix verification O(K N^3).
candidates.minimum_viability_test: For N=2 and N=4, beta equals 1, every row support is <=2, and independent RMSE is <=1e-12.

candidates.method: Hierarchical two-factor initialization followed by projected alternating continuous-complex updates; per row retain the two coefficients giving the best projected local objective, then globally polish.
assumptions: local projected updates reduce or preserve the accepted objective
multiple seeds partially sample nonconvex basins
candidates.objective: Minimize RMSE at each registered (N,K), then apply the common tie order.
candidates.complexity: Approximately O(sweeps*K*N^2) with sparse residual caching; naive fallback O(sweeps*K*N^3).
candidates.minimum_viability_test: At N=4,K=2, return a finite feasible chain and independent RMSE matching search RMSE within 1e-10.

candidates.method: Initialize from Butterfly pairings, then alternate continuous coefficient polishing with large-neighborhood row-support reconnection and separately optimized permutations.
assumptions: Butterfly provides a useful but nonexclusive initial topology
accepted reconnect moves preserve row support <=2
candidates.objective: Minimize RMSE and test whether topology search improves C/K at equal accuracy.
candidates.minimum_viability_test: At N=8,K=3, execute at least one legal reconnect proposal and retain a finite feasible incumbent.

problems.constraints: beta=1; q=3; real and imaginary parts of every factor entry lie in P3={0,+/-1,+/-2,+/-4}; no row-sparsity constraint; K>=1.
problems.data_split: No statistical split; full deterministic target for each N, shared byte-identically across candidates, with independently regenerated verification target.
problems.seed_policy: Deterministic quantization seed 0; stochastic challengers seeds 17,43,71 for every (N,K).
problems.budget: Global segmented budget; all challengers at equal (N,K) receive identical caps.
problems.tie_breaker: RMSE within 1e-12 ties, then lower C, lower K, lower wall_clock_s, lower seed, lexical candidate id.
problems.failure_rule: Apply global failure rule; any real/imaginary component outside exact P3 is CONSTRAINT_FAIL.
problems.fallback_rule: Keep q2-b0-onefactor-quantize if challengers do not improve the registered ordering.

candidates.method: Set K=1 and independently round each real and imaginary target component to its nearest P3 value using a fixed deterministic tie rule.
assumptions: K=1 is a legal positive layer count
componentwise nearest projection is deterministic
candidates.objective: Provide a simple feasible P3 reference.
candidates.complexity: O(N^2) construction and O(N^2) direct residual.
candidates.derivation: Original deterministic baseline: separability of squared Frobenius error at K=1 makes nearest componentwise P3 projection optimal within this restricted baseline class.
candidates.minimum_viability_test: At N=2, every real/imaginary component is exactly in P3 and metrics independently match.

candidates.method: Recursively select a P3 right factor by sparse-recovery-style greedy proposals, solve/update the left residual factor, project to P3, and finish with exact discrete coordinate polishing.
assumptions: recursive factorization can improve over one-factor quantization
accepted factors remain exactly in P3
candidates.complexity: Naive O(sweeps*K*N^3); cached proposals may reduce constants.
candidates.minimum_viability_test: At N=4,K=2, return exact-P3 factors and a finite independent RMSE.

candidates.method: Fit continuous multilayer factors with hierarchical projected alternating updates, quantize real/imaginary parts to P3, then use discrete block-coordinate and swap polishing.
assumptions: continuous solution is a useful initialization
post-projection polishing can recover quantization loss
variables: K dense P3 factors after projection
candidates.objective: Minimize final exact-P3 RMSE; pre-projection RMSE is diagnostic only.
candidates.minimum_viability_test: At N=4,K=2, perform both phases and verify every final entry is in P3.

problems.constraints: beta=1; q=3; every counted layer has at most two nonzeros per row; every real/imaginary component is in P3; pure permutations separate.
problems.data_split: No statistical split; the entire deterministic target is used for search and an independently regenerated target is used for verification.
problems.seed_policy: Baseline seed 0; challengers use seeds 17,43,71 for every (N,K).
problems.budget: Global segmented budget with equal challenger caps at each instance.
problems.tie_breaker: RMSE within 1e-12 ties, then lower C, lower K, lower wall_clock_s, lower seed, lexical candidate id.
problems.failure_rule: Apply global failure rule; row support >2 or any P3 component violation is CONSTRAINT_FAIL.
problems.fallback_rule: Keep q3-b0-quantized-butterfly unless a feasible challenger wins under the common ordering.

candidates.method: Use radix-2 Butterfly support and deterministically project every continuous real/imaginary coefficient to P3, followed by one fixed-order discrete coordinate pass.
assumptions: N is a power of two
Butterfly support is legal under row support <=2
variables: P3 coefficients on fixed Butterfly support
candidates.objective: Provide a reproducible feasible row-two P3 baseline.
candidates.complexity: O(N log N) construction; O(KN^3) dense verification.
candidates.minimum_viability_test: At N=4, all rows have support <=2, all components are in P3, and RMSE is finite.

candidates.method: Alternate exact P3 coefficient updates with single-row support swaps while preserving at most two nonzeros per row; accept only independently verified improvements.
assumptions: local discrete neighborhoods contain useful improvements
cached residual updates are exact within tolerance
candidates.minimum_viability_test: At N=4,K=2, complete a coefficient and support sweep without violating P3 or row support.

candidates.method: Build factors hierarchically, perform global discrete polishing, then use beam-ranked multi-row/multi-layer reconnect moves to escape fixed Butterfly structure.
assumptions: hierarchical initialization reduces bad local minima
large neighborhoods can improve fixed-support solutions
candidates.objective: Minimize final legal RMSE at equal budget.
candidates.minimum_viability_test: At N=8,K=3, produce a feasible incumbent and record at least one evaluated reconnect neighborhood.

problems.target: T=F_4 tensor F_8, dimension N=32, not F_32
problems.constraints: beta=1; q=3; every counted 32-by-32 layer has at most two nonzeros per row; components in P3; pure permutations separate.
problems.data_split: No statistical split; exact F4 tensor F8 is the full target. Verification regenerates F4 and F8 independently and hashes their Kronecker product.
problems.seed_policy: Baseline seed 0; challengers seeds 17,43,71 for each K.
problems.budget: N=32 global budget: 60 s baseline and min(900 s,15000 sweeps) for each challenger seed/K.
problems.tie_breaker: RMSE within 1e-12 ties, then lower C, lower K, lower wall_clock_s, lower seed, lexical candidate id.
problems.failure_rule: Apply global failure rule; using F32 or a target hash inconsistent with F4 tensor F8 is immediate TARGET_FAIL.
problems.fallback_rule: Retain q4-b0-kron-butterfly if neither challenger wins under the common ordering.

candidates.method: Construct P3-quantized Butterfly factors for F4 and F8, lift and compose them using Kronecker identities into counted 32-by-32 layers, then verify directly against F4 tensor F8.
assumptions: Kronecker identities are applied with consistent factor order
lifted layers preserve row support <=2
candidates.complexity: O(N log N) sparse construction; O(KN^3) dense verification for N=32.
candidates.minimum_viability_test: Verify target is unitary, max|F4 tensor F8-F32|>1e-3, and every lifted factor is legal.

candidates.method: Ignore Kronecker structure after target generation and run generic row-two P3 coefficient/support coordinate search directly on the 32-by-32 target.
assumptions: generic supports may outperform the structured baseline
local exact moves are evaluable within budget
candidates.objective: Minimize q4 RMSE at each K.
candidates.minimum_viability_test: At K=5, return a finite legal chain against the exact Kronecker target.

candidates.method: Start from the Kronecker-aware baseline, globally polish P3 coefficients, and allow beam-ranked cross-block row-support reconnect moves.
assumptions: Kronecker initialization is informative
cross-block reconnects can correct quantization error
candidates.objective: Minimize q4 RMSE while retaining exact constraints.
candidates.minimum_viability_test: Evaluate at least one legal cross-block reconnect and retain an independently verified incumbent.

problems.scope_note: Finite instances are computational evidence only; all-t claims require construction or proof.
secondary_metrics: q reported but never used as a tie objective
problems.constraints: beta=1; q is a positive integer in the registered search grid; every counted layer has row support <=2; coefficient components belong to P_q; C=qL; RMSE<=0.1 for eligibility.
problems.data_split: No statistical split; full deterministic target for each N. Independent verification regenerates the target and recomputes feasibility and the entire (C,K,RMSE) tuple.
problems.seed_policy: Baseline seed 0; challengers use seeds 17,43,71 for every (N,q,K), without early cancellation.
problems.budget: Global segmented budget; equal challenger caps at every (N,q,K). The full q/K grid is attempted unless a run itself fails or times out.
problems.tie_breaker: Among RMSE-feasible runs compare C, then K, then RMSE exactly as D-005; q is not a tie objective. If all three tie within 1e-12, use lower seed then lexical candidate id only for deterministic reporting.
problems.failure_rule: Apply global failure rule. RMSE>0.1 is INFEASIBLE, not PASS. If no feasible run exists, winner remains null and best infeasible RMSE may be reported separately.
problems.fallback_rule: If challengers do not improve the feasible lexicographic tuple, retain q5-b0-q1-butterfly; if the baseline is infeasible and no challenger is feasible, declare no feasible winner within budget.

candidates.method: For q=1, quantize a Butterfly chain to the free coefficient set and scan the registered K values; retain the best independently verified feasible tuple without presuming K=5.
assumptions: q=1 is a legal search value
all q=1 P1 complex combinations lie in the D-005 free set and therefore L=0 when used
candidates.objective: Find a reproducible zero-C feasible reference if one exists.
candidates.stop_condition: Complete all registered K or deterministic 60-second cap per K.
candidates.complexity: O(KN^2*|P1|^2) for a fixed discrete pass plus independent verification.
failure_modes: incorrect claim that K=5 is predetermined
candidates.minimum_viability_test: At N=2, verify every coefficient is in P1, L=C=0, and feasibility is computed independently.

candidates.method: Search every registered (q,K) using hierarchical initialization and exact discrete coordinate/support updates; retain only RMSE-feasible runs and rank them by (C,K,RMSE).
assumptions: the finite q/K grid is the declared computational scope
hierarchical initialization provides diverse legal incumbents
candidates.objective: Satisfy RMSE<=0.1, then minimize (C,K,RMSE); never use q as a tie objective.
candidates.stop_condition: Global stop rule per run; complete all registered runs.
candidates.minimum_viability_test: At N=4, run q=1 and q=2 for two K values and verify ordering ignores q after equal (C,K,RMSE).

candidates.method: Use the same q/K grid and seeds as c1, but alternate beam-ranked multi-row support reconnections with exact P_q coefficient polishing and incumbent pruning by feasibility plus a conservative lower bound.
assumptions: larger support neighborhoods can escape coordinate local minima
pruning never discards a tuple that can beat the incumbent under the implemented bound
candidates.objective: Find a better feasible (C,K,RMSE) tuple at exactly equal instance budget.
candidates.stop_condition: Global stop rule per run; complete all registered runs.
candidates.derivation: Original from-scratch candidate inspired only at the idea level by the user V6 memo; no V4-V6 factors, code, logs, RMSE, K, or C are inherited.
candidates.minimum_viability_test: At N=8,q=1,K=3, evaluate one multi-row reconnect, independently verify the incumbent, and retain every failed proposal reason.
